hook: The patent clerk who discovered relativity and E = mc², and changed how we see the universe.

pages.x: Albert Einstein was born in Ulm, Germany, in 1879, and grew up in Munich. When he was about five, his father showed him a compass. That the needle always pointed north amazed him: something hidden had to be moving it.
A myth says he failed maths. In fact he had taught himself calculus by 15. He hated his strict German school, left it, and finished school in Switzerland.
Unable to get a university job, he worked as a clerk in the patent office in Bern, checking inventions, and thought about physics in his spare time.

In 1905, aged 26, he published four papers. One showed that light comes in tiny packets. One proved that atoms exist. One set out special relativity, and one showed that E = mc²: mass and energy are two forms of one thing.
pages.fx: They founded modern physics, from quantum theory to nuclear energy. The packets of light explain how solar panels work.

pages.x: In 1915 he showed that gravity is the bending of space and time by mass. In 1919 astronomers watching an eclipse saw starlight bent by the Sun, just as he had said, and he became famous overnight.
pages.fx: It explains black holes and the expanding universe, and GPS satellites must correct for it to work.

pages.x: He won the Nobel Prize in Physics for 1921, not for relativity, but for explaining how light knocks electrons out of metal. He gave the prize money to his first wife, as he had promised in their divorce.
The Nazis hated him because he was Jewish, and burned his books. In 1933 he left Germany for good, and settled at Princeton, in the United States.
In 1939 he signed a letter to President Roosevelt warning that Germany might build an atomic bomb. It helped start the American bomb project. He later called it the one great mistake of his life.
He refused to wear socks, and in 1952 he turned down an offer to become president of Israel, saying he lacked the talent for dealing with people.
Einstein's theories of relativity and light changed how we understand space, time, energy and the universe. His name has become another word for genius.
pts: Showed that light comes in packets, a root of quantum physics
Won the Nobel Prize in Physics
